title: Basement Cleanout Services
h1: Basement Cleanouts That Give You Your Space Back

blocks.text: Basement Cleanouts That Give You Your Space Back
Years of buildup, cleared in a single visit — sorted, hauled, and swept.

items.title: Serving tenants, landlords & property managers across the GTA
Insured, uniformed crews experienced in condo & apartment buildings

c: Basements have a way of becoming the family archive nobody asked for. Old couches, broken exercise equipment, holiday bins, outgrown toys, paint cans, water-damaged boxes — it all drifts downstairs “for now” and stays for a decade. When the day finally comes to reclaim that square footage, the real obstacle isn’t deciding to do it; it’s the hundreds of trips up a narrow staircase with heavy, awkward loads.

That’s exactly the work our basement cleanout crews were built for. We bring the manpower, the equipment, and the truck, then carry every last item up and out while you simply point at what goes. Whether you’re finishing the basement, prepping a home for sale, dealing with flood-damaged contents, or just tired of the clutter, we start with a free upfront quote and finish with a clean, open floor. Homeowners across the Greater Toronto Area trust us because we make the job fast, fairly priced, and environmentally responsible.

blocks.text: Ten Years of Clutter, Gone Before Dinner

c: The hardest part of a basement cleanout is starting. Every box needs a decision, every piece of furniture needs two people and a plan for the stairs, and the pile never seems to shrink. That’s why so many basements stay full — and why our customers tell us hiring a crew was the difference between “someday” and “done.”

One call brings a full team to your door, often the very same day. We haul out old furniture and appliances, dusty exercise machines, filing cabinets, carpets, shelving, storage bins, renovation debris, and every unlabeled box in between. As we work, we separate what can be donated from what can be recycled, so charities get the usable goods and only genuine waste is discarded. Damp, musty, or flood-affected items are handled too — you don’t need to touch a thing.
As for pricing, basement cleanout costs depend on how much we haul, and you’ll get a firm number before a single item moves.
Want that basement empty this week?
Call us now at +1 647 922 5865 or book online at LiveJunkFree.ca.

blocks.text: Top-to-Bottom Basement Clearing – Stairs, Storage Rooms & All

c: What makes basements uniquely difficult is the geography: steep or narrow staircases, low ceilings, tight corners at landings, and single points of exit. Getting a fridge or a sofa bed down there was hard enough — getting it back up, along with everything else, is a genuine two-to-four-person job with the right straps and dollies.

Live Junk Free has emptied every kind of lower level: unfinished storage basements, finished rec rooms, basement apartments between tenants, cold cellars, crawl spaces, and utility rooms packed to the rafters. Whether the trigger is a renovation, a downsizing move, a flood recovery, a home sale, or an inherited property, we scale the crew and truck space to match what’s down there.

Our team plans the route before lifting anything — padding stair railings, protecting drywall corners, and laying runners across main-floor flooring so nothing upstairs pays the price for what’s leaving downstairs. Bulky items that won’t clear the stairwell get dismantled on the spot.

items: Complete clear-out – Storage areas, cold rooms, under-stair spaces, and utility corners emptied to the walls

items.q: 1) What kinds of items can you remove from a basement?
a: Nearly everything — furniture, appliances, exercise equipment, boxes, bins, carpets, shelving, electronics, tools, toys, and general clutter. The main exceptions are hazardous materials like paint, chemicals, and propane tanks, which we’ll help you direct to proper municipal depots.

items.q: 2) Can your crew manage narrow or steep basement stairs?
a: Yes — stairs are the core of what we do. Our teams use lifting straps, stair-climbing dollies, and coordinated two-to-four-person carries, and we pad railings and wall corners along the route. Oversized pieces are dismantled below before coming up.

items.q: 3) How long will my basement cleanout take?
a: A lightly filled basement is often done in one to two hours, while a packed, wall-to-wall space typically takes three to five. Nearly every job, regardless of size, is finished in a single visit with the right crew and truck.

items.q: 4) Do you handle flood-damaged or musty basement contents?
a: We do. Water-logged boxes, damp carpets, mildewed furniture, and post-flood debris are removed regularly by our crews and disposed of appropriately. It’s one of the most common reasons GTA homeowners call us after a storm or a burst pipe.

items.q: 5) Do I have to sort or organize anything before you come?
a: Not at all — arriving to an untouched basement is completely normal for us. Just set aside or clearly mark anything you’re keeping, and we’ll sort, carry, and haul everything else, including deciding what’s fit for donation versus recycling.

blocks.text: Locations We Serve With Our Basement Cleanout Services
Common Questions About Basement Cleanout Services

c: Basement cleanouts can involve everything from old furniture and boxes to heavy appliances, electronics, construction debris, and years of accumulated belongings. At Live Junk Free, we help homeowners across the GTA understand the cost, preparation, safety, and removal process before booking a basement cleanout. Below are answers to common questions about basement junk removal, difficult access, specialty items, and responsible disposal. Whether you’re decluttering, renovating, dealing with water damage, or clearing out a long-unused basement, these answers can help you plan the job with confidence.

items.q: Read What People Ask About Basement Cleanouts
a: 1. What is the average cost to clean out a standard unfinished basement?

The cost of a basement cleanout depends on the amount of junk, type of items, labour, accessibility, and disposal requirements. A lightly cluttered basement will generally cost less than one packed with furniture, appliances, boxes, and debris. Live Junk Free can provide an estimate based on the volume and type of items that need to be removed.
2. How much extra do companies charge if the basement stairs are narrow, steep, or winding?

Difficult basement access can increase the labour required to safely remove heavy or bulky items. Narrow, steep, or winding stairs may affect the overall cost depending on the number of items and the time needed for removal. Live Junk Free can assess the access conditions when providing your estimate.
3. Do cleanout services charge by the weight of the items or the volume of the truck?

Junk removal pricing varies between companies. The cost may be influenced by the amount of truck space your items occupy, the type and weight of materials, labour, and disposal requirements. Live Junk Free provides pricing based on the specific scope of your basement cleanout.
4. Is it more expensive to clean out a basement that has water damage or flooding?

A basement affected by flooding or water damage may require additional work, especially if materials are wet, contaminated, or difficult to handle. Certain situations may also require specialized restoration or remediation before junk removal can safely take place.
5. Are there extra fees for removing heavy, outdated basement appliances like chest freezers or old furnaces?

Large appliances can require additional labour and specialized disposal or recycling. Chest freezers, furnaces, and similar heavy items may therefore affect the cost of a basement cleanout depending on their size, weight, and disposal requirements.
6. Can I get a discount if I move some of the lighter basement items up to the garage myself?

Moving items to an easily accessible location can reduce the amount of time and labour required for removal. However, pricing depends on the overall volume and scope of the cleanout. Ask Live Junk Free about your specific situation when requesting a quote.
7. How much does it cost to remove a large pool table or ping-pong table from a basement?

The cost depends on the table’s size, weight, construction, and accessibility. Pool tables may also require disassembly before they can safely be moved upstairs. Live Junk Free can assess the item and access conditions to determine the appropriate removal approach.
8. Is there a minimum charge for a company to come out for just a few basement items?

Many junk removal companies have minimum service charges for smaller jobs. The minimum can vary based on location, labour, truck requirements, and the type of items being removed. Contact Live Junk Free to discuss your specific removal needs.
9. Do cleanout quotes include the cost of dump fees and recycling taxes?

This depends on the company and the materials involved. Live Junk Free aims to provide clear pricing so customers understand the expected costs associated with their basement cleanout before the work begins.
10. What is the price difference between a junk removal company and a specialized hoarder basement cleanout?

A hoarding cleanout can require significantly more labour, sorting, removal, and disposal than a standard basement cleanout. The cost depends on the volume of belongings, accessibility, condition of the space, and whether specialized remediation is required.
11. Will a cleanout service enter a basement that has active mold or mildew?

Minor mildew may not necessarily prevent removal, but significant mold contamination can create health and safety concerns. Specialized mold remediation may be required before a standard junk removal crew can safely enter and work in the basement.
12. How do cleanout crews handle spaces with severe spider infestations or rodent droppings?

Severe pest infestations or significant rodent contamination may require pest control or specialized cleaning before junk removal. Customers should disclose known infestations so the appropriate safety measures and service requirements can be determined.
13. Can a cleanout company safely remove old paint cans, chemicals, and motor oil from a basement?

Paint, chemicals, motor oil, and other hazardous materials may require specialized disposal and are not always accepted by standard junk removal companies. Let Live Junk Free know about these materials before the appointment so proper disposal options can be discussed.
14. What happens if the crew discovers asbestos insulation around basement pipes?

Asbestos-containing materials should not be disturbed or removed by a standard junk removal crew. If suspected asbestos is discovered, stop work around the material and contact a qualified asbestos professional for assessment and removal.
15. Will a company clean out a basement that currently has standing water or damp floors?

Standing water can create electrical, structural, mold, and contamination risks. Water removal and restoration may need to happen before a junk removal crew can safely enter the basement and remove damaged belongings.
16. Do cleanout workers wear protective gear or respirators for dusty, dirty basements?

Safety requirements depend on the condition of the basement and the materials being removed. Basic protective equipment may be used when appropriate, but heavily contaminated environments may require specialized remediation professionals with specific PPE and respiratory protection.
17. How do they prevent bringing pests or fleas from the basement into the main house during removal?

Crews should be informed about any known pest or flea problems before work begins. In severe cases, professional pest treatment may be necessary before belongings can be safely removed and transported through the home.
18. Can they clean up sewage backup residue as part of the cleanout?

Sewage contamination requires specialized cleanup because of potential biological hazards. Standard junk removal should not be treated as sewage remediation; contaminated areas may need to be professionally cleaned and disinfected before ordinary removal work begins.
19. Will a cleanout service refuse a job if the basement structure looks unsafe?

Yes, safety comes first. If stairs, floors, ceilings, electrical systems, or other structural elements appear unsafe, the crew may need to stop or decline the job until the hazard has been addressed by a qualified professional.
20. What should I do if I suspect there is lead paint on the basement walls they are working near?

Do not scrape, sand, or disturb suspected lead-based paint. Inform the cleanout company before work begins and consider having the material assessed by a qualified professional, particularly if the paint is deteriorating.
21. Can a basement cleanout crew dismantle a built-in wooden bar or old shelving?

Some basic dismantling and removal may be possible depending on the construction and service requested. Structural demolition or extensive built-in removal may require a specialized demolition contractor.
22. Do cleanout services remove heavy gym equipment like treadmills or weight racks from downstairs?

Yes, many basement cleanout services can remove heavy exercise equipment such as treadmills, weight benches, and racks. The crew will consider the equipment’s size, weight, and access route when determining how it can be safely removed.
23. Will they haul away old carpeting, subflooring, or drywall ruins after a flood?

Some construction and water-damaged materials may be accepted as part of a cleanout, depending on their condition and disposal requirements. Heavily contaminated or hazardous materials may require specialized handling.
24. Do companies offer a sweep-up service to leave the basement floor clean after junk removal?

Some junk removal services provide basic sweeping or tidying after items have been removed. A full deep cleaning, sanitization, or restoration service is generally separate and should be arranged if required.
25. Can a cleanout service help me sort through decades of boxes to find family heirlooms?

Customers should ideally sort through boxes before the removal crew arrives when important or sentimental belongings may be mixed with unwanted items. Live Junk Free can remove the items you identify for disposal, while valuables and heirlooms should be clearly separated and marked to keep.
26. Will they take apart an old piano that is stuck in the basement?

Pianos are extremely heavy and can be difficult to remove through basement stairs or narrow access points. Depending on the piano and removal conditions, specialized dismantling may be required. Discuss the piano with Live Junk Free before scheduling the removal.
27. Do they handle old firewood, coal leftovers, or construction debris?

Many general basement cleanouts can include common construction debris and unwanted materials. However, coal, treated materials, chemicals, or other specialty waste may have specific disposal requirements, so the items should be identified before removal.
28. Can I hire a service to just move items from the basement to a storage unit on-site?

This depends on the service provider and the type of job requested. If you need items relocated rather than disposed of, confirm whether the company provides moving or transportation services in addition to junk removal.
29. Do cleanout companies take old electronics, tube TVs, and computer monitors?

Many junk removal companies accept electronic waste, including older televisions and computer equipment. These items should be handled through appropriate e-waste recycling or disposal channels rather than placed with regular household garbage.
30. Will they remove rusting tools and scrap metal from an old basement workshop?

Yes, scrap metal, unwanted tools, and workshop items can often be included in a basement cleanout. Where possible, recyclable metal can be separated for appropriate recycling rather than sent to general disposal.
31. How do workers avoid scratching the walls or damaging the ceiling when carrying items up basement stairs?

Professional crews use careful lifting and carrying techniques and assess the route before moving large items. Bulky belongings may need to be dismantled to safely navigate narrow stairs, doorways, and corners.
32. What happens if a heavy item falls and breaks the basement staircase during the cleanout?

Crews take precautions to prevent damage, but accidents can happen during difficult removals. Before the job begins, discuss fragile stairs, narrow access points, and unusually heavy items with the service provider so an appropriate removal plan can be established.
33. Do I need to be home while the crew is working in the basement?

Not necessarily. If the company permits unattended cleanouts, you may be able to arrange authorized access and provide clear instructions about what should be removed. Confirm the access and payment arrangements with Live Junk Free beforehand.
34. How long does it typically take a 3-person crew to clear out a heavily cluttered basement?

There is no fixed timeframe because every basement is different. The amount of clutter, number of large items, stairs, distance to the truck, sorting requirements, and disposal needs can all affect how long the cleanout takes.
35. Will the company bring their own lighting if the basement bulbs are burnt out or missing?

Customers should provide safe lighting where possible before the appointment. If the basement is extremely dark or unsafe to access, the crew may need to determine whether the area can be worked in safely before starting.
36. Do cleanout trucks need to park right next to the basement bulkhead or cellar door?

Parking as close as legally and safely possible can make the removal more efficient. However, trucks do not always need to be directly beside the basement entrance, provided there is a safe and practical path for carrying items to the vehicle.
37. What is the best way to organize a basement before a cleanout crew arrives?
Separate everything into

b: keep, donate, recycle, sell, and remove

a: categories. Remove valuables and important documents, clearly mark anything that should stay, and make pathways accessible so the crew can safely reach the items being removed.
38. How do I decide what to keep, donate, or throw away when clearing out a childhood basement?

Start with sentimental and genuinely useful belongings, then consider whether each remaining item is worth storing. Items in good condition may be donated or sold, while broken, damaged, or unusable belongings can be placed in the removal pile.
39. Can you give me a weekend timeline checklist to clean out my own basement?

Start Saturday morning by sorting everything into keep, sell, donate, recycle, and remove piles. Work room-by-room, schedule disposal or donation pickups, move selected items out of the basement, and use Sunday to finish sorting, remove remaining junk, and sweep the space.
40. Where can I donate large basement items like old tools or vintage furniture?

Usable tools, furniture, and household items may be donated to local charities, reuse organizations, community groups, or other organizations that accept them. Before donating, check whether the organization accepts the specific item and whether pickup is available.
